### Describe the bug

On gfx1151 (Strix Halo), `decode_attention_fwd(..., has_mla=True)` with Lk 576 / Lv 512 (v aliasing k, as the MLA KV cache does) returns NaN or badly wrong output rows for long sequences when the batch is ragged. The error is ~4 against an fp32 reference; bf16 rounding alone is ~1e-2. Which rows fail changes from run to run with identical inputs, which points at a read of uninitialized or racing memory.

What triggers it (main @ `0afb736`, `get_num_kv_splits_triton` with max splits 64, which `_mla_decode_kv_splits_cap` picks on this 40-CU part):

Lengths  | Splits per seq  | Bad runs
--- | --- | ---
`[1000] * 24`, `[9000] * 2`, `[9000] * 4`, `[3, 700, 9000]`  | 63, 64, 36, (1/5/64)  | 0/8, 0/3, 0/3, 0/3
`[9000] * 3 + [3]`  | 64 x3, 1  | 3/3 (rows of the 9000-token seqs)
`[3, 700, 9000] * 2`  | (1/5/64) x2  | 3/3
